patient_information: A 71-year-old Japanese man, born and currently living in the Kyushu district of southern Japan. He is clinically well with no reported complaints.
chief_complaint: Referral for further work-up of an asymptomatic nodular lesion in the right lung.
history_of_present_illness: The patient was found to have a lung lesion two years prior during a routine health check. Initially, the lesion was of a linear shape and was followed regularly. On a recent follow-up visit, chest radiography and CT scan revealed that the linear shadow had transformed into a nodular lesion approximately 2 cm in diameter. The patient remained asymptomatic throughout this period.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is a lifelong resident of the Kyushu district in southern Japan, a region where paragonimiasis is endemic. He has no history of travelling overseas.
physical_exam: Physical examination was normal. The chest was clear on auscultation.
labs_and_diagnostics: A full blood count revealed a white blood cell count of 6.5 x 10^9/L with an eosinophil percentage of 8.3% (total eosinophil count 0.54 x 10^9/L), indicating mild eosinophilia. Total IgE was elevated at 185.7 U/mL. Liver function, renal function, electrolytes, LDH, and CRP were all normal. Serologies for Cryptococcus Ag, Aspergillus Ag, and β-D-glucan were negative, as was a QuantiFERON test for tuberculosis. A chest radiograph and CT scan identified a nodular lesion of about 2 cm in the right lung. An FDG-PET-CT showed increased FDG uptake in this lesion. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) cytology was negative for malignant cells and acid-fast bacilli, and tumor markers were negative. The diagnosis was confirmed with a multiple-dot ELISA which was strongly positive for P. westermani.
differential_diagnosis: The primary differential diagnoses for a lung nodule with increased FDG uptake were pulmonary tuberculosis and lung cancer. Systemic endemic mycoses were considered but deemed unlikely as the patient had no travel history to endemic areas outside of East Asia. Given the patient's origin in southern Japan, eosinophilia, and elevated IgE, pulmonary helminth infection, specifically lung fluke infection (paragonimiasis), was strongly suspected.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with a 3-day course of oral praziquantel at a dose of 25 mg/kg three times daily. Following treatment, the lung lesion gradually faded and eventually disappeared. His serum antibody titre for P. westermani also declined, indicating a successful response to therapy.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis is pulmonary paragonimiasis caused by the lung fluke Paragonimus westermani. This was established based on the patient's epidemiological risk as a resident of an endemic area in Japan, the clinical presentation of an asymptomatic lung nodule, and laboratory findings of peripheral eosinophilia and elevated IgE. The diagnosis was definitively confirmed by a strongly positive multiple-dot ELISA for P. westermani and further supported by the complete resolution of the lung lesion and decline in antibody titers following treatment with praziquantel.
